profile.reading:
DartPoints operates a data center at 7139 Florida Boulevard in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, designated BTR02, positioned by the company as a geographic-redundancy companion to its adjacent BTR01 facility roughly a dozen building numbers away on the same street and power grid connection, intended to give enterprise customers a second Baton Rouge option for disaster-recovery purposes. This facility traces its origin to Venyu, a company DartPoints describes as having operated for more than 30 years as Louisiana's premier data center infrastructure and cloud services provider, which DartPoints acquired on May 2, 2023 from its then-parent company, REV. REV's own published company history confirms it was formed through a 2019 merger of RTC, a Louisiana telephone cooperative founded in 1935 in Reserve, and EATEL, an Ascension Parish telecom provider that built one of the first fully fiber-to-the-home networks in the country and had itself acquired a company called Vision Communications in 2011, with the merged entity rebranding as REV in 2022. The direct organizational link explaining exactly when Venyu became EATEL's data center and colocation arm was not independently confirmed from any source reached this session. The BTR02 facility draws 3 megawatts of utility power against a 400-kilowatt critical IT load, backed by 4,000 kilowatts of generator capacity and cooled by 760 tons of N+1 redundant capacity. DartPoints' own materials give inconsistent data-hall square footage figures for this specific building across different pages, a discrepancy noted honestly here rather than resolved by picking one figure. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed, and no Uptime Institute Tier certification level is stated for this building.

DartPoints markets itself company-wide as serving more than 900 enterprise customers, including universities, hospital systems, and Fortune 500 companies, across its roughly 11 data centers spanning 5 states.

reading.body:
DartPoints Baton Rouge 2 publishes 3 megawatts of IT capacity, making it the largest mapped data center facility in Louisiana and accounting for nearly 40 percent of the state's published data center load.

The facility is one of three DartPoints properties whose real estate the operator acquired outright in April 2025 when NOVA Infrastructure took majority control of the company with more than 250 million dollars in combined growth capital. This shift signals sustained investment in regional capacity outside major metropolitan markets. At 3 megawatts, the site holds roughly 75 racks assuming 40 kilowatts per rack, a common density for AI training workloads.

DartPoints operates 11 facilities across 10 regional markets and serves more than 900 enterprise customers including Fortune 500 companies, universities, and hospital systems. The company emphasizes AI-ready infrastructure and high-density deployment. The data does not disclose the facility's total power supply, electrical grid connection capacity, or headroom for expansion beyond the currently published 3 megawatts. Whether this campus can grow depends on factors the operator has not revealed.
